The Two Golden Orientations

90% of mistakes are just left/right confusion. Fix the orientation first.

⭕ Circle, all facing the CENTRE: a person's left = clockwise direction, right = anticlockwise. (Sit at the north seat facing inward — you are facing South, and facing South your left hand points East, which is the clockwise way round the table.)
⭕ Circle, all facing OUTSIDE: everything flips — left = anticlockwise, right = clockwise.
📏 Row facing NORTH (away from you): their right = your right. Row facing SOUTH (toward you): their right = your left — mirror image.
🔢 Ranking formulas: Rank from other end = Total − rank + 1 · Total = left rank + right rank − 1 · People between two positions = |difference| − 1.
🧩 Solving strategy: start with the most "fixed" clue (opposite, middle, end, exact position), place it, then chain the relative clues one by one. Never start with a vague "not adjacent" clue.
